theme: For God alone my soul waits in silence
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 62. It is a psalm of quiet trust by David. Notice the repeated word “alone” and how it deals with the temptation to trust in people, power, or wealth.
settingTheScene: Psalm 62 is a psalm of David, probably from a time when enemies were plotting against him. It is a calm psalm in the middle of threat. The key word is “alone”: God alone is my rock. In Corinth, believers were tempted to trust in human leaders and human wisdom. This psalm calls us back to rest in God alone.
observation: “For God alone my soul waits in silence; from him comes my salvation” (v. 1).
“He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be greatly shaken” (v. 2).
“For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him” (v. 5).
“On God rests my salvation and my glory; my mighty rock, my refuge is God” (v. 7).
“Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us” (v. 8).
“Those of low estate are but a breath; those of high estate are a delusion” (v. 9).
“If riches increase, set not your heart on them” (v. 10).
“Once God has spoken; twice have I heard this: that power belongs to God” (v. 11).
interpretation:
David opens, “For God alone my soul waits in silence; from him comes my salvation.” The Hebrew has a sense of silence and stillness: the soul is quiet before God. He is not silent because he has no words, but because he is resting. “He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be greatly shaken.” The word “alone” appears six times in the psalm. It narrows trust to one object.

Then he addresses his enemies: “How long will all of you attack a man to batter him, like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?” They plan to thrust him down from his high position. They take pleasure in falsehood; they bless with their mouths, but inwardly they curse. In the face of this, David speaks to his own soul: “For God alone, O my soul, wait in silence, for my hope is from him.” He repeats verses 1 and 2 almost word for word, with a slight change. In the first, “I shall not be greatly shaken.” In the second, “I shall not be shaken.” His confidence grows as he preaches to himself.

Verse 8 turns outward to the people: “Trust in him at all times, O people; pour out your heart before him; God is a refuge for us.” Prayer is pouring out the heart. Then David exposes the false refuges: “Those of low estate are but a breath; those of high estate are a delusion; in the balances they go up; they are together lighter than a breath.” People of any rank, high or low, cannot hold up your weight. Neither can wealth: “Put no trust in extortion; set no vain hopes on robbery. If riches increase, set not your heart on them.” Money is not evil, but it is a poor god.

The psalm ends with God’s word: “Once God has spoken; twice have I heard this: that power belongs to God, and that to you, O Lord, belongs steadfast love. For you will render to a man according to his work.” God is both strong and kind. Power without love would be terrifying; love without power would be useless. God has both.

The cross shows both. The power of God is displayed in weakness; the love of God is shown in sacrifice. This is the paradox that Paul preached in Corinth. Rest in God alone, and pour out your heart to him.
connection: Psalm 37:7 says be still before the LORD and wait patiently for him. Psalm 46:10 says be still and know that I am God. Isaiah 30:15 says in returning and rest you shall be saved. Lamentations 3:25-26 says it is good to wait quietly. Matthew 6:19-24 warns about treasures and serving two masters. 1 Timothy 6:17-19 addresses the rich. Jeremiah 17:5-8 contrasts trust in man with trust in the LORD. Romans 2:6 echoes verse 12. Philippians 4:6-7 speaks of prayer and peace.
application:
Sit in silence for five minutes today. Practice waiting on God alone.

Ask where you are trusting in people, position, or money. Name one and entrust it to God.

Pour out your heart to God in prayer today, without editing.
prayerPrompts: Wait on God in silence for a moment, and then tell him what you hope for.
Thank him that he is your rock and fortress.
Pour out your heart to him.
